title: How does your phone reach the hub when you are away from your desk?
context: The hub runs on your PC and only answers on that PC (localhost). Away from your desk you cannot see cards or answer them, so agents stall on permission prompts and decisions. Whatever opens it up must keep everyone else out: the hub can run commands on your machine through its agents.

options.name: Private network for your devices
options.summary: Install Tailscale on the PC and the phone. The hub gets an https address that only your own signed-in devices can open; nothing is reachable from the open internet. On the phone it is the same hub page, added to the home screen like an app.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='60' width='90' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='65' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Phone</text><rect x='215' y='60' width='90' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='260' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>PC</text><text x='260' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>hub</text><rect x='125' y='40' width='75' height='100' rx='10' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><line x1='112' y1='90' x2='213' y2='90' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='213,90 206.7,93.0 206.7,87.0' fill='currentColor'/><text x='162' y='160' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>your devices only</text></svg>
pros: Nothing exposed to the internet at all
Full hub on the phone: cards, threads, board, live map
Free for personal use; no domain or server to run
Gives the https the phone needs for notifications
cons: One more app on the PC and the phone
Works only on devices you have signed in
The PC has to be on and awake
options.effort: Small: install two apps, one command, plus a short hub change to trust the address

options.name: Public address behind a sign-in
options.summary: A Cloudflare tunnel publishes the hub at a subdomain of a domain you own, with Cloudflare Access asking for a one-time email code before anything loads.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='15' y='60' width='80' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='55' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Phone</text><rect x='120' y='50' width='90' height='80' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><text x='165' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Sign-in</text><text x='165' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>gate</text><rect x='235' y='60' width='70' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='270' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>PC</text><text x='270' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>hub</text><line x1='97' y1='90' x2='118' y2='90' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='118,90 111.7,93.0 111.7,87.0' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='212' y1='90' x2='233' y2='90' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='233,90 226.7,93.0 226.7,87.0' fill='currentColor'/><text x='165' y='160' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>on the internet</text></svg>
pros: Opens from any browser, even one you have never used
cons: The hub sits on the open internet; safety rests on the sign-in gate
Needs the domain's DNS moved to Cloudflare
More to set up and to keep right

options.name: No remote page: chat only
options.summary: Keep the hub on the PC only. Away from your desk, everything comes and goes through a chat app (decision 19 picks which).
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='60' width='90' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='65' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Phone</text><text x='65' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>chat app</text><rect x='215' y='60' width='90' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='260' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>PC</text><text x='260' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>hub</text><rect x='120' y='120' width='80' height='40' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><text x='160' y='137' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Chat</text><text x='160' y='151' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>service</text><line x1='60' y1='122' x2='118' y2='140' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='118,140 111.1,141.0 112.9,135.2' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='213' y1='120' x2='202' y2='140' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='202,140 202.4,133.0 207.7,135.9' fill='currentColor'/></svg>
pros: Nothing on the PC is opened up
Works in an app you already check
cons: Only what fits in a chat message: no board, no live map, no full decision pages
Every card's contents pass through the chat company's servers

criteria.name: Contents stay with you
criteria.note: B passes through Cloudflare; C through the chat company

recommendation: It gives you the whole hub on the phone without putting anything on the internet, and it is the least to set up. It also provides the secure address that phone notifications (decision 19) need.
